description: Where the poll row comes from: "538 raw-polls (2023 release)" (1998-2022), "538 polls pages (archived)" (2023-24), "NYT polls files" (2025-26)
Poll id in the source (538 numeric ids; NYT uuids)
Question id in the source. One question per poll and race: likely voters over registered voters over adults
Election cycle: the even year, pooling the preceding odd year (2023-24 = 2024)
Race type: Pres-G (president, general), Pres-P (presidential primary), Sen-G, House-G (district), House-G-US (generic ballot), Gov-G
Race id (538's for 1998-2022; the NYT results race id or a constructed key for 2023-26)
State postal code, "US" for national, or state-district for House races (e.g. "NY-3")
Pollster name
538 pollster rating id (blank for pollsters 538 never rated; averages weight those by name)
Partisan/internal flag (D, R, I) where the source gives one; blank otherwise
Median field date
Election date
Days from the median field date to the election (0-21)
Sample size
Candidate 1: the Democrat when a Democrat and a Republican finished first and second, else the winner
Candidate 1's party
Candidate 1's share in the poll
Candidate 1's share of the vote (percent of all votes cast)
Candidate 2: the Republican in Democrat-vs-Republican races, else the runner-up
Candidate 2's party
Candidate 2's share in the poll
Candidate 2's share of the vote
cand1_pct - cand2_pct
cand1_actual - cand2_actual
|margin_poll - margin_actual|
margin_poll - margin_actual, Democrat-vs-Republican races only (positive = polls overstated the Democrat, i.e. Republicans underrated)
